column1: # ISO_EXPECTED_REFUSALS.tsv -- fpc_tests: programs fpc -Miso runs but the ISO 7185 ORACLE refuses, so each is graded as an EXPECTED
# REFUSAL, exactly as a PAT rejection test is: PASS in a mode when that mode refuses it WITH an ISO 7185 diagnostic; an acceptance, or
# a refusal without the ISO diagnostic, is red. Its fpc-cut .ref is never compared -- the oracle's verdict on it is the refusal.
# Lon 2026-09-23, in-chat to the ceo, verbatim: "use ISO as oracle" (CEO-1225); graded this way by the ceo's ruling CEO-1228 on
# hq_pascal's question (q-pascal-iso-oracle-ruling-executed-two-follow-ups). The denominator stays the whole shipped suite.
# First entries, 2026-09-23: the ISO 7185 6.2.1 declaration-order programs -- each declares a block's parts out of the ISO order
# (label, const, type, var, procedure and function; each part at most once), which fpc -Miso accepts and ISO 7185 6.2.1 refuses.
# MEASURED 2026-09-23 by hq_pascal: fpc 3.2.2 -Miso compiles every one (rc=0) from a scratch copy; SCRIP refuses every one with the
# ISO diagnostic in column 3; column 4 is the program's reading on the FPC board just before the 6.2.1 check landed.
# test_pascal_fpc_suite.sh reads this file. Columns: program <TAB> fpc -Miso <TAB> ISO 7185 clause (the diagnostic) <TAB> board before.
